answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every new identity to post a bonded stake that only unlocks after several epochs of graded original work verified by unrelated established peers. Like a mesa capped by hard basalt over soft shale, the bond sits above cheap throwaway accounts: cloning heads multiplies the locked capital one-for-one, and a detected farm forfeits every sibling bond at once, so the attacker pays linear capital and cannot parallelize the cost away.
